description: Attribution taxonomy for the paper book: which sleeve a position belongs to, which class that sleeve rolls up into, and which macro regime the sleeve is an expression of. This is a REPORTING map, not a trading rule — it never gates a fill. Correlated-position caps come from config/correlation_buckets.json; this file exists so P&L can be read as 'the hard-asset book made money and the risk-on book didn't'.

$resolution_rules.order: sleeves are evaluated in declaration order; the first whose membership contains the ticker wins
$resolution_rules.membership: union of (a) the watchlist_tickers of the referenced `theme` in config/asset_themes.json, (b) the members of each referenced correlation `bucket`, (c) the coin list named by `crypto_universe` in config/crypto_universe.json, and (d) the explicit `tickers` list here
$resolution_rules.unmatched: a ticker no sleeve claims is looked up in config/ticker_sectors.json and routed by `$sector_fallback` below; only a name nothing anywhere knows falls through to `unclassified`, which is then reported honestly rather than silently folded into another sleeve
$resolution_rules.explicit_wins: the declared membership above always beats the sector fallback — that is how IREN and WULF are read as the crypto miners they are rather than the Capital Markets names a screener files them under
$resolution_rules.resolution_time: read time, not entry time — re-classifying a ticker here corrects history instead of leaving old positions mis-bucketed

$sector_fallback.note: Why this exists: the membership above is an allowlist of names this desk had already formed an opinion about — the index ETFs, the megacaps, the thematic baskets. The copy books trade whatever their channel posts, which is mostly small-cap momentum nobody had written down, so roughly sixty names sat in `unclassified` for no better reason than that. A ticker's own sector is enough to place it, and config/ticker_sectors.json carries that for every name the books have touched.
$sector_fallback.order: by_industry is checked first, then by_sector. Industry is the one that carries the thesis — `Aerospace & Defense` is a defense name whether the screener filed its parent sector as Industrials or Technology, and `Other Industrial Metals & Mining` is the critical-minerals trade while its parent, Basic Materials, also holds the gold miners.

hard_assets.label: Hard assets
hard_assets.note: Real things and the equities that dig them up. The debasement / commodity-inflation expression.

equities.label: Equities
equities.note: Listed equity risk, sliced by sector and theme.

crypto.label: Crypto
crypto.note: Digital assets and their listed proxies.

rates_fx.label: Rates & FX
rates_fx.note: Duration and dollar — the macro hedges.

cash.label: Cash
cash.note: Dry powder held deliberately, not by accident.

other.label: Unclassified
other.note: Nothing has been mapped yet. A large number here is a to-do, not a category.

sleeves.label: Crypto — majors
sleeves.note: The coins come from config/crypto_universe.json `majors`, so a listing change arrives here through scripts/refresh_crypto_universe.py rather than by hand. The tickers are the listed proxies — treasuries, ETFs and the miners, which a sector screener files under Capital Markets and which are nothing of the sort.

sleeves.label: Crypto — non-major alts
sleeves.note: Every other Coinbase-listed coin. The books no longer OPEN these — see `book_tradeable` in prices/symbol_map.py — but the replayed history holds seventeen of them, and reading that P&L as ordinary crypto beta would flatter the majors. Kept as its own sleeve so the alt tail is attributable on its own.

sleeves.label: Copper & industrial metals
sleeves.note: The electrification / grid-buildout expression. Absent from asset_themes.json, which is why three of the book's first twelve positions had no classification.

sleeves.label: Power & grid buildout
sleeves.note: Storage, generation and the wires — the demand side of the same electrification trade `industrial_metals` owns the supply side of. Absent until the copy book bought EOSE and NRGV and neither had anywhere to go.

sleeves.label: Staples, utilities & real estate
sleeves.note: The three bond-proxy sectors travel together on rates; splitting them would make three sleeves that always say the same thing.
